subject: Usage credits vs model surcharge — structure review
messages:
From: Anu Singh <anu@brightship.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage credits and rate questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — we reviewed Redwood's RFP response and landed on a few follow-ups specifically around how usage credits and per-token discounts interact with model-specific premiums. A couple of concrete items:

- BrightShip expects to use chat (assist) heavily for customer support workflows and embeddings for semantic search. How do you apply discounts across embeddings vs chat? Do they consume the same credit buckets?
- For premium model families (Redwood-Delta / other larger models), the RFP shows a 1.8x multiplier vs base. Is that a fixed multiplier or negotiable inside a committed volume?
- We also want to understand whether unused monthly credits rollover or whether you offer one-time ramp credits for the first 3 months.

Attached is our RFP excerpt for pricing (BrightShip_RFP_Q3.pdf). We are targeting a decision in the next two weeks and will need a committed pricing term for procurement.

Can we get a short linesheet that shows (a) 12/24 month commit tiers, (b) blended per-token examples at target volumes, and (c) how embeddings are billed relative to chat?

Thanks,
Anu
Procurement Manager — BrightShip

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Anu Singh <anu@brightship.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 13:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage credits and rate questions

Hi Anu — appreciate the clear asks and the RFP excerpt. Short answer up front: embeddings and chat consume the same underlying token accounting, but we provide specialized per-unit price points for embeddings that often map to lower effective $/query because of encoding differences. Model premiums are configurable inside committed deals — they are not an immutable surcharge.

I attached a concise summary (redwood_pricing_summary_v3.pdf) and sketched two practical options below so your procurement team can compare quickly:

Option A — Standard committed tiers (12/24m)
- Baseline chat (gpt-equivalent standard): $0.0025 / 1k tokens at $250k annual commit
- Embeddings: listed at $0.0015 / 1k tokens (separately shown but draws from same credit pool)
- Premium models: model multiplier 1.75x (can be reduced to 1.5x for higher commits)
- Unused monthly credits: do not roll over; we provide a 3-month ramp credit equal to 7.5% of the first year commit, applied in quarterly installments

Option B — Blended bucket (recommended for variable usage)
- Single blended $/1k token per month driven by model mix caps. Example at 10B tokens/mo: blended $0.0019 /1k tokens (chat-heavy)
- Embedding queries are priced as a discounted line item in the example (effective 20–35% cheaper per typical query pattern)

Requests:
- Marissa / Jordan: can you weigh in on whether we can offer a 1.6x cap on premium models for a 24-month $500k+ commit? Also need formal approval path for the ramp credits and non-rollover policy.

Anu — happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow to run through examples and finalize lines.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage credits and rate questions

Kim / Jordan — quick internal note and suggested concession math. Quoting Kim's options below for context.

> Premium models: model multiplier 1.75x (can be reduced to 1.5x for higher commits)
> Unused monthly credits: do not roll over; we provide a 3-month ramp credit equal to 7.5% of the first year commit
\Suggested commercial approach (to make RFP comparison favorable):
- Tier A (12m, $250k commit): keep 1.75x premium multiplier, offer 10% off first-year list for chat tokens (one-time rebate applied to first invoice). Provide 5% ramp credits (smaller but faster).
- Tier B (24m, $500k commit): reduce premium multiplier to 1.6x, embedded pricing moved to explicit $/embed (0.9x of chat $/token assumption), provide 7.5% ramp credits + 6% annual volume rebate if they exceed forecast by >20%.
- Blended / Flex: offer a blended example for their expected 70/30 chat/embed mix; commit can be dynamically reconciled monthly with a true-up at quarter-close.

I put math and line-item examples in proposal_linesheet.xlsx — key numbers: at 10B tokens/month chat-heavy, our blended offer at Tier B yields ~38% TCO improvement vs their incumbent pricing in RFP.

Approval asks to Jordan: can finance sign off on the 6% annual rebate conditional? If yes, I'll prepare a term sheet for signature (DocuSign ready). If not, recommend swapping the rebate for an additional ramp credit.

Marissa
Director, Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Anu Singh <anu@brightship.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Firm linesheet and next steps — BrightShip commit proposal

Anu — thanks for the patience while we pulled internal approvals. Below is a consolidated term sheet and next steps.

Committed proposal (brightship preferred):
- Term: 24 months
- Commit: $525,000 annual (billed monthly) — annualized $1,050,000 over 24 months
- Base chat rate (blended example): $0.00185 / 1k tokens (applies to standard model usage)
- Embeddings: explicit $0.0012 / 1k tokens (draws from same token accounting; cheaper effective per typical query)
- Premium models: 1.6x multiplier to base chat rate (1.6 * $0.00185 = $0.00296 /1k tokens)
- Ramp credits: 7.5% of first year commit applied in quarterly credits during first 12 months
- Annual volume rebate: 6% rebate if actual annualized usage exceeds committed spend by >20% (true-up at year close)
- Unused monthly credits: do not roll; true-ups at quarter close with carry-forward limited to 1 month if over-achieved in prior month (one-time exception)
- Cancellation / early termination: standard mutual termination with 60-day notice; remaining committed credits billed pro rata

Attachments: BrightShip_Commit_Term_Sheet.pdf (term sheet for signature)

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/secure/BR-2026-0421

Next steps:
1) Procurement: confirm acceptance of term sheet by EOD Thu
2) Legal: we will push a limited redline contract if procurement asks; expect 3–5 business days for standard SLAs
3) Kickoff: once signed, we will provide a technical onboarding checklist and a 4-week migration playbook to minimize startup token spend.

Anu — happy to discuss any of the line items live. If BrightShip prefers a 12m instead of 24m, we can reprice but the premium multiplier will move to 1.7x and ramp credits reduce to 5%.

Best regards,

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
